source.title: In the name of art, go with the flow
source.author: Darryl Levings
source.publicCitation: Darryl Levings, 'In the name of art, go with the flow,' The Kansas City Star, November 15, 2007, pp. A1, A4.
source.identityNote: This is the canonical identity of the published article. The supplied PDF is a preservation artifact, not another source.

observations.text: The article was the illustrated lead story on the Kansas City edition front page and continued on page A4.

observations.text: The project began with an idea by James Burkart.

Two bicycles linked to a paddle wheel supplied human power.

observations.text: The raft left the West Bottoms on July 21, 2007.
Several friends were aboard at departure.
At publication the crew was somewhere south of Baton Rouge.
The crew had passed the 1,000-mile marker.
The raft generally moved at approximately two to four miles per hour.
The article supplied the project's long-form title.
A living experience on the rivers was a stated purpose.
Meeting people along the rivers was a stated purpose.
Mattingly described an intention to preserve spontaneity rather than rely on maps or books.

observations.text: Mattingly described technology as optional rather than required.
Friends joined route segments around St. Louis, Memphis, and Vicksburg.
The crew often stopped for food and water.

observations.locator: A4, column 2, sentence beginning 'Police, fire, sheriff'

observations.locator: A4, column 2, paragraph beginning 'Fifteen miles north of Vicksburg'

observations.locator: A4, column 2, paragraph beginning 'Unsuitable design and configuration'

observations.locator: A4, column 2, concluding Coast Guard paragraph

observations.text: People in Vicksburg took in and fed the crew.
The article named Paul Kelly Loyacono as providing free legal help.

observations.attribution: Paul Kelly Loyacono, quoted by Darryl Levings

observations.text: Loyacono helped the crew find jobs in substitute teaching, being a coffee barista, and labor with home renovators.
A large group saw the crew off from Vicksburg.
The crew had been in Natchez on the Thursday before publication.
Fog cost the crew three half-days tied up, without locating each delay.
The crew expected to encounter salt water below New Orleans.
The crew did not know whether they would encounter salt by New Orleans.
The crew did not expect to see the Gulf from the raft.
James Burkart described the Kansas City river as invisible space.

observations.text: The article reports that the crew lifted the sagging bow, added cones for resistance, brought oars aboard, and added a marine radio before resuming travel.

claims.text: The article attributes the expedition idea to Jamie and documents Jamie, Libby Hendon, and Laura Mattingly traveling collectively on a reclaimed-material, bicycle-powered raft for more than 1,000 miles from Kansas City into Louisiana.

The article documents a collectively operated improvised technical system that adapted after a 51-day interruption through local hospitality, legal assistance, raft retrieval, work support, repairs, and added safety and communication equipment.

The article supports a participatory method built around lived river experience, encounters, invitations aboard, and Jamie's attributed hope for cultural connection between Kansas City's West Bottoms and Delta communities.

antiClaims.text: Jamie alone designed, built, steered, operated, or completed the expedition.
antiClaims.reason: The article names a collective crew and wider participation and support.

antiClaims.text: This article proves that the raft reached salt water or the Gulf of Mexico.
antiClaims.reason: The mid-voyage report preserves endpoint uncertainty.

antiClaims.text: The newspaper provides a complete route or stop chronology.
antiClaims.reason: It supplies selected locations and incidents rather than a route log.

antiClaims.text: The named travelers are the complete participant, builder, host, helper, or support roster.
antiClaims.reason: The article also reports friends, hosts, legal help, work, retrieval assistance, and a sendoff.

antiClaims.text: The article establishes measured cultural, civic, community, environmental, or policy outcomes.
antiClaims.reason: It reports intentions and encounters without an outcomes study.

antiClaims.text: The article provides engineering certification or blanket regulatory approval.
antiClaims.reason: It reports objections, a pause, modifications, and a later legal return.

antiClaims.text: Possession of the PDF grants permission to republish the pages, article body, or photographs.
antiClaims.reason: Copyright, photograph rights, and depicted-person consent were not cleared.

antiClaims.text: Front-page placement establishes endorsement, audience reach, hiring value, or cultural impact.
Fourteen is the combined count of contacts with every authority named in the article.
antiClaims.reason: The count applies to Coast Guard encounters; other agencies are separately uncounted.

sourceLimitations.text: The article was published while the expedition was underway.
sourceLimitations.consequence: Later endpoint and duration claims require separate later evidence.

sourceLimitations.text: The report names selected places and incidents but is not a route log.
sourceLimitations.consequence: Exact stops, dates, and final landing remain open.

sourceLimitations.text: The report does not allocate every design, construction, navigation, repair, organizing, documentation, or support task.
sourceLimitations.consequence: Collective credit and role uncertainty remain attached.

sourceLimitations.text: River and cultural-connection statements are attributed to Jamie, not community consensus.
sourceLimitations.consequence: Portfolio use must preserve attribution and possibility.

sourceLimitations.text: The article contains no participant census or measured outcome study.
sourceLimitations.consequence: Encounters cannot become reach, adoption, or impact metrics.

sourceLimitations.text: No republication or photograph-use rights were established.
sourceLimitations.consequence: Only metadata and bounded paraphrase enter the repository.

sourceLimitations.text: The PDF container was created in 2008 while the newspaper publication date is in 2007.
sourceLimitations.consequence: Artifact metadata must not replace publication metadata.

sourceLimitations.text: Layout-aware extraction is a reading aid, not the newspaper's visual form.
sourceLimitations.consequence: Placement, captions, and column order require rendered-page review.

sourceLimitations.text: Contemporary reports disagree whether the consequential Coast Guard stop occurred on September 15 or September 18.
sourceLimitations.consequence: Atlas retains the conflict without averaging or silently selecting a date.
